method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill (and references/regulative.md), from the seat of the individual to whom the Rules are applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18 and the rulings on negatives of 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05 (JUST FALSE where the text says no, NOTHING with a NOTHING-kind tag where it does not answer); Order 3's counting in a dates module, six regulative rules (rr 14.02, 14.04, 15.08(2), 29.03, 33.07/33.08, 85.03) run by EVALTRACE inside exported questions that take only plain facts, and four question modules with their own @export questions; the parent Act (Supreme Court Act 1986 ss 33E, 33J) and the Legal Identity of Defendants (Organisational Child Abuse) Act 2018 (ss 7(3), 13) restated narrowly with their sections; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Supreme Court (General Civil Procedure) Rules 2025 (Vic), S.R. No. 85/2025, Version No. 003 (incorporating amendments as at 1 January 2026), as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/supreme-court-general-civil-procedure-rules-2025.txt (committed text sha256 5a7e31c55401557d05bbfb38d5a447cd585187b0d771b6b27dc5d2e692f549ed), converted from the Word file saved by hand by the owner on 2026-11-07; in operation from 8 September 2025, revoking the Supreme Court (General Civil Procedure) Rules 2015 (S.R. No. 103/2015) by r 1.03(2) and Schedule 1

seat: the party: the individual who is a party to a civil proceeding in the Supreme Court of Victoria, usually the person bringing a personal injury or group claim (injured worker, road accident victim, patient, survivor of child abuse, group member, a minor or person under disability through a litigation guardian), and, where the Rules put a step on the other side, the individual answering it (defence, discovery, the defendant's medical reports, a summary judgment affidavit)
